subject: Handoff: measurement rules & prompt pack for Streaming SLO qualification

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: measurement rules & prompt pack for Streaming SLO qualification

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and the artifacts attached to kick off the Streaming SLO qualification: 

What we recorded from the call:
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 120ms for 512-token requests (user-facing tail).
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline steady-state of 200 concurrent requests (sustained), spike test to 400 for 5 minutes to simulate promo traffic.
- Streaming behavior: partial tokens should be delivered in <100ms per chunk for the first 3 chunks; overall streamed response time should not exceed the non-streaming baseline by >20% under the steady-state load.
- Error budget: target error rate <0.5% (we'll formalize threshold in the measurement spec).

What I'm attaching here (first pass):
- streaming-prompt-pack-v1.csv (sample prompt set and token accounting)
- harness-runbook-v1.md (how to spin up the eval harness and repeat runs)
- measurement-specs-v1.pdf (definitions for metrics, warmup, steady-state, and reproducibility checklist)

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the acceptance criteria above (latency/throughput/err) or flag changes.
2) We run a short smoke qualification from Redwood to validate fixture and credentials (2–4 hrs).
3) Schedule the full run (2x 10-minute steady-state windows with ramp and spike). Proposed window: Apr 12–13 (you said that week looks good).

Please review the attachments and the prompts (especially the streaming prompt cases — they're marked with CHUNK tags). If any of your team needs a different token mix, tell us and we'll regenerate the prompt pack.

A couple of notes for the perf engineers:
- We recommend recording a traffic replay (replay file format described in harness-runbook-v1.md) to ensure reproducibility.
- For streaming tests, the harness will emit both first-byte and per-chunk latencies; we recommend analyzing both for SLO alignment.

If this all looks good, say "go" and we'll drop test credentials into the Drive folder and run the smoke test next business day.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear recap and the artifacts. A few quick clarifications from our side before we greenlight the smoke run:

1) Instrumentation: can Redwood accept client-side trace IDs (we'll emit a request-id header) and include that in result traces so we can join logs locally? Our perf team prefers end-to-end correlation.
2) Cold vs warm: we need separate measurements for cold-start (overnight idle) vs warmed-up instances. Can the harness support a cold-start sweep?
3) Spike pattern: the 2x spike for 5 minutes is fine; can you also run a short burst test (10s at 10x) to simulate flash sales?

We looked at the prompt pack — good coverage. We'll also send a small supplemental token mix (higher-embedded payloads) for one of the streaming scenarios.

We'll aim to review the attachments with perf-eng on Monday and confirm the Apr 12–13 window. If you can outline the smoke-run deliverables (what outputs we'll get and where results land), that will help our ops team.

Thanks,
Alyssa Carter

Subject: Re: Handoff: measurement rules & prompt pack for Streaming SLO qualification

Hi Alyssa — Marcus from Redwood's performance team here. Quick responses and a concrete run recipe below.

On instrumentation: yes, please send request-id as X-Req-Id header (we'll echo it in logs and include it in the harness output csv). We'll also add a correlation id column in the results.csv so you can join with client logs.

Cold vs warm: harness supports both. Proposed warmup procedure: 5 minutes of ramp (linear) to target concurrency followed by a 10-minute steady-state for baseline. For cold-start sweep:
- Recreate instance from a cold image (runtime with empty KV cache), then run 20 single-shot requests spaced 30s apart to capture first-request latency distribution. Repeat for 3 instances.

Steady-state & spike pattern:
- Ramp: 0 -> target over 300s (linear).
- Steady-state: 10 minutes at target concurrency (200).
- Spike: jump to 400 concurrency for 5 minutes.
- Burst: 10s at 2000rps (we'll translate to concurrent clients using the harness reel) to exercise throttles.

Measurement definitions (we'll publish verbatim in measurement-specs-v1.pdf but copying the core here):
- First-byte latency: time from request send to first token received. Reported as p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Per-chunk latency: latency between successive streamed chunks (average and tail).
- End-to-end token time: total duration until final token.
- Throughput: completed responses/sec during steady-state window.
- Error rate: % of requests with non-2xx or streaming truncation.

Reproducibility checklist:
- Harness run config (git tag + manifest) attached.
- Prompt pack versioned and checksummed (md5 in header).
- Seeded RNG for any stochastic prompt augmentation.
- Traffic replay file included for exact replay.

Example harness commands (linux):
- ./harness run --config runs/acme-steady-200.yaml --out results/acme-steady-200.csv
- ./harness analyze results/acme-steady-200.csv --metrics first_byte p95 per_chunk_mean

Deliverables from smoke run:
- raw results CSV (includes X-Req-Id, timestamps, per-chunk timings)
- summary pdf with p50/p90/p95/p99 and error rate + annotated charts
- replay file used for the run

I'll also drop a tiny example of the results header into the Drive folder so your team can validate join keys.

Let us know if the burst (10s @ 10x) is required for the qualification run or if you want that separate.

Thanks
Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
